title: Pakistan takes the One China policy into its airspace
gist: Pakistan briefly barred Taiwan's China Airlines and EVA Air from its airspace citing the One China policy — a restriction even China does not impose — before reversing it with access only until 27 March 2027. Hashmi reads it as either Beijing-directed pressure or a loyalty signal by Islamabad as it courts Washington, and warns it could set a precedent for using commercial aviation as a pressure tool on Taiwan.

insights.claim: Pakistan barred Taiwanese carriers China Airlines and EVA Air from transiting its airspace, with Defence Minister Khawaja Asif saying the aviation division follows the One China policy and only mainland China is allowed.
insights.speaker: Sana Hashmi
insights.so_what: Introduces a new operational risk channel for Taiwanese airlines' Europe/Middle East routes.

themes.theme: Pakistan-Taiwan ties and One China interpretation

insights.claim: Pakistan-Taiwan ties are minimal: just over 900 Pakistani nationals live in Taiwan, there has never been a representative office, and there are no direct flights; the only South Asia-Taiwan air link is the Taipei-Delhi route, scheduled to resume on 1 December.
insights.speaker: Sana Hashmi
insights.so_what: Pakistan bears near-zero economic cost from anti-Taiwan gestures, making them cheap signals.
insights.locator: Pakistan and Taiwan have few substantive

insights.claim: The One China policy is interpreted differently by countries — some adherents keep trade ties and unofficial offices in Taiwan — and it does not entail denying overflight to Taiwanese commercial airlines, which is a civil aviation matter.
insights.speaker: Sana Hashmi
insights.so_what: Stretching One China into civil aviation is a novel escalation worth monitoring among Beijing-aligned states.

insights.claim: In April, Seychelles, Mauritius and Madagascar withdrew overflight permissions for President Lai Ching-te's planned trip to Eswatini, Taiwan's only remaining African diplomatic ally — but restricting a presidential flight differs from banning commercial airlines.
insights.speaker: Sana Hashmi
insights.so_what: Overflight denial is an expanding tool of Taiwan isolation.

themes.theme: Motives: Beijing pressure or loyalty signalling

insights.claim: One explanation is that China asked Pakistan to impose the ban to reinforce the One China policy, discourage engagement with Taiwan and demonstrate Beijing's influence over partners, possibly as an extension of grey-zone activities.
insights.speaker: Sana Hashmi
insights.so_what: If Beijing-directed, expect replication by other close partners.

insights.claim: A second explanation is that Pakistan acted on its own to show loyalty to China while seeking closer ties with the United States, with the Mecca Pact adding to Islamabad's incentive to reassure Beijing.
insights.speaker: Sana Hashmi
insights.so_what: Pakistan's US pivot is creating friction it feels compelled to offset with symbolic pro-China moves.
